key_insight: Multi-turn code generation can be treated as a one-step recoverable MDP, enabling a contextual bandit formulation that captures most benefits of online RL while leveraging offline data to reduce cost and instability.
problem_solved: How to get the performance advantages of online RL for multi-turn code generation without the high training cost and instability of full online RL, and while making effective use of offline datasets.
method: Reformulate multi-turn code generation as a one-step recoverable Markov decision process so each decision can be treated as a contextual bandit problem.
Train a contextual bandit learner that leverages large offline code-revision datasets for reward signals and policy learning, avoiding repeated full episode rollouts.
Optionally integrate limited online interactions or off-policy corrections to refine the policy while keeping training cost and instability low.
impact: Provides a practical middle ground between offline and online RL for LLM-driven code generation: lower compute and more stable training than full online RL while retaining performance gains, enabling wider adoption in real-world development pipelines.
